Ternium Mexico Announces $350 Million Investment to Boost Steel Production

Ternium Mexico SA de CV has unveiled plans for a $350 million investment to expand its steel production facilities in the northern state of Nuevo León, signaling continued confidence in the Mexican steel sector and the country’s industrial prospects.

The company, part of one of Latin America’s leading steel producers, said the funds will be allocated over the next two years to increase capacity at its Pesquería plant. The expansion will add an estimated 1 million metric tons per year to Ternium Mexico’s output, focusing on advanced steel grades for the automotive, appliance, and construction markets.

“This investment underscores our commitment to Mexico’s industrial development and our customers’ growing demand for high-quality steel products,” said Adrián Varela, General Director of Ternium Mexico SA de CV, at a press conference in Monterrey. “The expansion is expected to create over 600 direct jobs and approximately 2,000 indirect positions during construction and ramp-up phases.”

Industry analysts welcomed the announcement, noting that domestic steel demand remains robust amid nearshoring trends and infrastructure projects. “Ternium’s move is a vote of confidence in the Mexican manufacturing ecosystem,” said Ana Torres, metals sector analyst at Grupo Consultor Industrial. “It also reflects the company’s strategy to offer specialized materials required by modern industry.”

The Cámara Nacional de la Industria del Hierro y del Acero (CANACERO) described the project as “a milestone for national steelmaking” and highlighted the importance of continued private investment for maintaining Mexico’s competitive edge.

Local officials in Nuevo León expressed optimism about the economic impact. “This initiative will strengthen our region’s position as a manufacturing hub and generate valuable employment for our communities,” stated State Secretary of Economy Roberto Salinas.

Ternium Mexico said the expansion will include state-of-the-art environmental controls and energy efficiency upgrades, in line with its sustainability goals.

Construction is set to begin in the third quarter of this year, with completion targeted for late 2026. The expansion will bring Ternium Mexico’s total annual steelmaking capacity in the country to more than 6 million metric tons.
